[untitled BTM module] Granulocyte development and activation is the theme here: a transcriptional core that commits myeloid progenitors to the neutrophil lineage, a cytokine receptor that drives their expansion, and signalling and cytoskeletal components that let mature cells respond. [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation.

Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.
